ruling.recommended_action: Hand the prepared case file to a human reviewer (Trust & Safety) as a safety incident: attach the complaint, the driver's written statement (F4), the empty in-app chat log (F3), the GPS record (F1, F2) and both profiles (F5, F6); do not issue any refund, fee waiver or driver violation, and do not flag or sanction either account pending the review; serve SAFE-4 interim measures only if the reviewer directs them.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a safety case filed by the rider. The complaint states that the driver repeatedly commented on the rider's body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe during the trip. The trace's SAFE-1 screen is settled (✓): a complaint describing inappropriate conduct and a rider feeling unsafe routes to a human, and the only allowed outcome is escalate [F3][SAFE-1].

The safety screen: I read the only text on the file — the complaint itself and the driver's post-trip statement "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened" [F4]. The complaint alleges unwanted sexual/personal comments and a request for the rider's number, i.e. harassment and a person feeling unsafe; nothing in the chat (there is none) or in the statement contains a threat, but the allegation of inappropriate conduct is squarely within SAFE-1. Safety concern is therefore suspected, and under SAFE-3 this tier may not rule, assign fault or recommend a resolution. I make no finding on whether the alleged conduct occurred: the rider's account appears only in the complaint and the driver's denial only in a statement written after the trip, with no in-app chat to corroborate either side [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-3].

What is disputed and what to check: whether the driver made body-related comments and asked for the rider's number during the approximately 17-minute trip (pickup 12:50, drop-off 13:07). The reviewer should weigh the rider's first-person account against the driver's general denial [F4], note that the in-app chat log is empty so there is neither corroboration nor an exculpatory record [F3], consider whether any call recording or other trip audio exists (the record shows none), and weigh credibility using both profiles — rider 129 d, 4.5, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F5]; driver 327 d, 4.67, 999 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F6]. No fraud flag is recorded on either party [F5][F6][TH-3].

The driving record is normal and decides nothing here: actual 17.1 km versus optimal 17.2 km (−0.1 km, −0%) and 17.0 min versus 23.6 min estimated [F1][F2]. The fare is a fixed $35.70 with no fare or excess-distance issue, so no monetary remedy arises; the amount is null and no route or billing clause bears on the safety allegation.

Evidence: the record contains no chat, no call recording and no other contemporaneous record of the alleged conduct, so the account cannot be verified either way [F1][F3][F4][TH-4]. The file goes up unruled, with no presumption in favour of either party, and no account action against the driver at this tier.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety incident: complaint alleges unwanted body comments, a request for the rider's number and that the rider felt harassed and unsafe (SAFE-1); under SAFE-3 the automated tier may not rule, assign fault or recommend a resolution, and the record (empty chat F3, no call recording, driver's denial F4) cannot verify either account.

rejected_claims.reason: Factually correct as a description of the complaint, but it asks the court to treat the alleged conduct as established; the conduct rests on the complaint alone, with no chat or call record (F3) and the driver's general denial (F4), so under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 the court escalates without finding the conduct proved.

Accepted that this is a safety indicator routing to a human under SAFE-1 (F3), but the rider's account is a statement, not a system record, and the empty chat log (F3) neither corroborates nor contradicts it; no finding of fact can be made at this tier (SAFE-3).

Accepted that F4 is a claim and does not by itself rebut the rider's account; that is precisely why the record is inconclusive and the file escalates under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 rather than being decided for the rider.

Granted in outcome — escalation is the ruling — but the rider's framing that her account is credited and the driver's is not goes beyond the record: no fault is assigned to either party (SAFE-3), and no account flag attaches to the driver under RD-6 (F6).

The profile readings (F5, F6) are accurate, but profiles never decide a case; they go only to the credibility the human reviewer weighs, and no fraud flag or RD-6 repeat deviation exists on this record (F6).
Accepted: a harassment/personal-safety allegation is screened to a human under SAFE-1 and no fault is assigned by the automated tier (SAFE-3); this is the basis of the escalation.
The absence of in-app chat (F3) is neutral, not exculpatory; an empty chat log cannot show that nothing was said aloud, so it neither proves nor disproves the allegation (SAFE-1).

The GPS record (F1, F2) is indeed an ordinary shortest-path trip, but RD-1 is a route-deviation clause and has no bearing on a safety allegation; normal driving is consistent with both accounts and refutes neither (SAFE-1).
Accepted as to the mechanism: the automated tier prepares and hands over the case file and may not rule, determine fault or recommend a resolution (SAFE-3).

Accepted as to money: the fare is a fixed $35.70 with no excess distance (F1), so no monetary remedy is computed and the amount is null; this does not dispose of the safety allegation, which escalates under SAFE-1.
Accepted: profiles cannot decide the case (F5, F6) and no RD-6 account flag attaches to the driver, whose record shows 0 upheld deviations (F6); credibility remains for the human reviewer under TH-3.

ruling.evidence_gap: No in-app chat, call recording or other contemporaneous record of the trip's communication exists (F3 shows an empty chat log; the only accounts are the rider's complaint and the driver's post-trip statement F4), so whether the alleged comments and number request occurred cannot be settled from the record.
